name: Lawn Fertilizer Rate Calculator
seoTitle: Lawn Fertilizer Rate Calculator — Formula & Results
seoDesc: How much fertiliser to spread on a lawn, from the nitrogen rate you want and the analysis on the bag. Free lawn fertilizer rate calculator: enter your values
summary:
How much fertiliser to spread on a lawn, from the nitrogen rate you want and the analysis on the bag. It returns product per 1 000 ft², product needed, bags needed and nitrogen applied overall, and the panel shows all of them at once.

Turf wants about 0.5–1 lb of actual nitrogen per 1 000 ft² per application, and the bag's first number tells you how much product that is. Every result is derived from the boxes you fill in, so changing one input updates the whole panel at once. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Lawn Fertilizer Rate
sections.html:
Product (lb) = area ÷ 1 000 × N rate ÷ (N% ÷ 100). A season of 2–4 lb N per 1 000 ft² is split across the growing season

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
N ratepounds of actual nitrogen per 1 000 square feetlb/1000 ft²
N%the first number in the fertiliser analysis, e.g. 24 in 24-0-11%
1 000 ft²about 93 m², the standard unit of turf recommendationsft²

sections.title: How do I use the Lawn Fertilizer Rate?
sections.html:
The form asks only for what the formula needs — nothing is optional decoration.

  1. Measure the lawn area in square feet (an acre is 43 560 ft²).
  2. Enter the nitrogen rate you want and the first number from the bag's analysis.
  3. The pounds of product, the number of bags and the season's total nitrogen are shown.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: lawn area of 5,000 ft², nitrogen per application of 1 lb N/1000 ft², nitrogen in the product of 24%, bag size of 50 lb.

Substituting them into the formula gives product per 1 000 ft² of 4.17 lb, product needed of 20.83 lb, bags needed of 0.4167, nitrogen applied overall of 5 lb, nitrogen over a season of 4 lb/1000 ft².

The arithmetic is the page's own: change one box and the result moves by the amount the formula implies, which is the quickest way to convince yourself the tool is honest.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
A raw figure only means something next to the bands it is normally judged against. Here is the scale that goes with this one:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
0.5 lb N/1000 ft²Lightshaded or low-maintenance turf
0.75 – 1 lbStandardthe usual rate per application for a home lawn
over 1.5 lbToo muchburn risk, thatch and runoff; split it into two applications

  • The rate that matters is actual nitrogen, not product weight. A 24-0-11 bag delivers a quarter of its weight as nitrogen, which is why 1 lb of N needs about 4 lb of product.

  • Total seasonal nitrogen for cool-season grass is 2–4 lb per 1 000 ft², split into three or four applications; warm-season grass wants 2–3 lb.

  • Sweep anything that lands on paving back onto the lawn — nitrogen on hard surfaces goes straight to the storm drain.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
The arithmetic is simple; the inputs are where things go wrong. The usual culprits:

  • Setting the spreader by product weight instead of nitrogen rate, which over-applies the cheap high-analysis products.
  • Applying a high-nitrogen product in midsummer heat, which burns the turf.
  • Feeding in late autumn in a cold climate, which feeds the snow mould rather than the grass.

faq.q: How much 24-0-11 do I need per 1 000 ft² for 1 lb of nitrogen?
How often should I fertilise a lawn?
faq.a: Three to four times a year for cool-season grass, at 0.5–1 lb N per 1 000 ft² each time.
No. Beyond about 1.5 lb per application the grass burns, thatch builds up and the surplus runs off.

faq.q: What does the Lawn Fertilizer Rate actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns product per 1 000 ft², product needed, bags needed and nitrogen applied overall. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.
